verdict: GO on all four round-1 items (no open blocker); round 1 kept intact and a Round 2 section appended. Each fix was verified by breaking it: resolver->'.ts' reddens verify-dist at D3 only (1 of 6) and the node suite at 416/417 (W3), restored byte-identical (1af54349); every D1-D6 reddens when its own dist/ artefact is removed; the two-gate deadlock surface was exercised with 28 requests measured waiting on the global gate while holding tenant slots - all 32 settled in 1043 ms, no hang, slots drained to 0/0, next request 208 ms, and grep shows one tenant-then-global acquire site and the reverse release; the continuation performs zero INSERTs and spends nothing (row deltas 0/0/0), cannot create a purchase (no_redemption), and Max-Age == cexp-iat with the render at cexp+grace; bundle_verify refuses all three shapes, each with a negative control. Two new majors: the E-28 register is file-scoped, and bursts of >=32 simultaneous buyers lose 28-42% of downloads to 503s.
false_refusal: 0/30 (0.0%) at 10/min, 0/60 (0.0%) at 20/min, 0/120 (0.0%) at 40/min - Poisson arrivals, 300-800 ms renders calibrated to a real 40-page PDF's 583 ms p50 under 8-way concurrency; also 0/40 for 40 buyers in 10 s. The defect is burst density, not rate: 24 at once = 0/24 in one run (max 1954 ms, 4 ms inside budget) and 3/24 (12%) in another; 28 -> 1/28; 32 -> 9/32 (28%); 36 -> 8/36 (22%); 40 -> 14/40 (35%); 48 -> 20/48 (42%). All reason='timeout' except 4 'queue' at 48; every refused buyer keeps uses=0 and exactly one denied_watermark row, so a 503 costs a reload, not an entitlement. Verdict on it: not a defect at 10/20/40 per minute, a product defect from ~32 simultaneous shoppers.
top_defect: S3R2-1 (Major, gate): the E-28 register is file-scoped - DIST_SITES is matched against occurrence.file, so a ninth runtime-path site appended to app/main.ts left E28-1/E28-2/E28-3 all green at 15 occurrences over 8 rows; the class that produced a 100% download outage can re-enter through render.ts or main.ts unnoticed. Fix: key the claim on (file, resolvedBy) or (file, line range) and compare counts. Runner-up: S3R2-2, the >=32-simultaneous false refusals above.
